He played [[college basketball]] for the [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason Patriots]] and the [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette Golden Eagles]]. Kolek was drafted as the 34th pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], but was traded to the Knicks on draft night. ==High school career== Kolek grew up in [[Cumberland, Rhode Island]], and initially attended [[Cumberland High School (Rhode Island)|Cumberland High School]].{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Koch|title=RI native Tyler Kolek playing for Marquette at The Dunk vs. PC|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2022/01/29/rhode-island-native-tyler-kolek-marquette-university-providence-college-basketball/9267683002/|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=January 29, 2022|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He transferred to [[St. George's School (Rhode Island)|St. George's School]] before the start of his senior year. Kolek was named the Rhode Island Gatorade Boys Basketball Player of the Year as a junior after averaging 18.6 points, 8.4 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 2.5 steals per game.{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Rueb|title=St. George's junior Kolek named R.I. boys basketball Gatorade Boys Basketball Player of the Year|url=https://www.newportri.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/03/15/st-georges-junior-kolek-named-ri-boys-basketball-gatorade-player-of-year/5698263007/|work=[[The Newport Daily News]]|date=March 15, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]] over offers from [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon]], [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]], [[Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball|Holy Cross]] and [[Vermont Catamounts men's basketball|Vermont]].{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Koch|title=St. George's guard, Cumberland native Tyler Kolek commits to|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/college/2019/09/17/st-georges-guard-cumberland-native-tyler-kolek-commits-to-george-mason/2765943007/|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=September 17, 2019|access-date=March 7, 2023}} ==College career== [[File:Tyler Kolek passing to a teammate from George Mason vs. Fordham at Eagle Bank Arena in Fairfax VA, February 10, 2021 (Patrick Rouin - All-Pro Reels Photography).jpg|thumb|Kolek with [[George Mason University]] in 2021]] Kolek began his college career at [[George Mason Patriots men's basketball|George Mason]].{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Kayata|title=Homecoming for Cumberland's Kolek |url=https://turnto10.com/sports/content/homecoming-for-cumberlands-kolek|website=[[turnto10.com]]|date=January 14, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He was named the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]] Rookie of the Year as a freshman after averaging 10.8 points, 3.6 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game.{{cite web|first=Bill|last=Koch|title=George Mason transfer Tyler Kolek Marquette Shaka Smart|url=https://www.providencejournal.com/story/sports/2021/04/14/george-mason-transfer-tyler-kolek-marquette-shaka-smart/7230318002/|work=[[The Providence Journal]]|date=April 14, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Following the end of the season, head coach [[Dave Paulsen]] was fired{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Paulsen out after six seasons at George Mason|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31076809|website=ESPN.com|date=March 16, 2021|access-date=March 27, 2024}} and Kolek entered the NCAA transfer portal.{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Kayata|title=Cumberland's Kolek enters transfer portal|url=https://turnto10.com/sports/content/cumberlands-kolek-to-enter-transfer-portal|website=[[WJAR|TurnTo10.com]]|date=March 19, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Kolek ultimately transferred to [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|title=Atlantic 10 freshman of year Tyler Kolek transfers to Marquette|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2021/04/14/atlantic-10-freshman-year-tyler-kolek-transfers-marquette/7230231002/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=April 14, 2021|access-date=March 7, 2023}} He averaged 6.7 points per game and led the [[Big East Conference]] with 5.9 assists per game in his first season with the Golden Eagles.{{cite web|title=Cumberland's Kolek continues to excel at Marquette, earns Big East Player of Week honors|url=https://www.valleybreeze.com/sports/cumberlands-kolek-continues-to-excel-at-marquette-earns-big-east-player-of-week-honors/article_9990be54-a1dc-11ed-ade3-33284d8806d7.html|work=The Valley Breeze|date=February 2, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}} Kolek was named the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big East Player of the Year]] and first team All-[[Big East]] as a junior.{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|title=Marquette's Tyler Kolek, Oso Ighodaro, Kam Jones earn Big East honors|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/03/05/marquettes-tyler-kolek-oso-ighodaro-kam-jones-earn-big-east-honors/69973679007/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=March 5, 2023|access-date=March 7, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Steele|title=Big East honors Marquette's Tyler Kolek and Shaka Smart as conference's basketball player and coach of year|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/03/08/marquettes-tyler-kolek-and-shaka-smart-big-east-top-player-and-coach/69983049007/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=March 8, 2023|access-date=March 9, 2023}} He was also named the Most Outstanding Player of the [[2023 Big East men's basketball tournament|2023 Big East tournament]] after averaging 18.7 points, seven rebounds and five assists in the three games.{{cite web|title=Marquette aims to douse upset bid by 15-seed Vermont|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/marquette-aims-to-douse-upset-bid-by-15-seed-vermont/|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=March 14, 2023|access-date=March 20, 2023}} Kolek averaged 12.9 points, 7.5 assists, 4.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals over 36 games on the season.{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Tucker|title=Men’s college basketball preseason All-Americans: Edey, Kolek lead The Athletic’s list|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5001990/2023/10/30/college-basketball-all-americans-zach-edey-tyler-kolek-hunter-dickinson/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 30, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} Kolek was named the preseason Big East Player of the Year as well as to multiple preseason All-American teams entering his senior season.{{cite web|title=Marquette's Tyler Kolek is Big East preseason player of year|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2023/10/24/marquettes-tyler-kolek-is-big-east-preseason-player-of-year/71298607007/|url-access=subscription|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=December 8, 2023}} ==Professional career== Kolek was selected with the 34th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], however, he was subsequently traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for the draft rights of [[Dani Díez]] and second-round picks in 2027, 2029 and 2030.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Acquire Three Future Second-Round Draft Picks in Exchange for 34th Selection Tyler Kolek|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-three-future-second-round-draft-picks-from-knicksin-exchange-for-34th-selection-kyle-kolek|website=NBA.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} On July 5, 2024, he signed with the Knicks.{{cite web|title=Tyler Kolek Signed by Knicks|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/tyler-kolek-signed-by-knicks|website=NBA.com|date=July 5, 2024|access-date=July 5, 2024}} Kolek made his NBA debut on October 22, in a 132–109 loss to the [[2024–25 Boston Celtics season|Boston Celtics]], scoring three points.{{cite web|title=New York Knicks at Boston Celtics Box Score, October 22, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410220BOS.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}} Throughout his rookie season, he has been [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[Westchester Knicks]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Westchester Knicks Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Westchester-Knicks/40/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 17, 2024}} On January 1, 2025, Kolek appeared in a rare double-header for the Knicks and their G League team, the Westchester Knicks. Kolek scored 36 points and 11 assists for the Westchester Knicks and just hours later scored two points and four assists for the New York Knicks.{{cite web|title=Tyler Kolek gives Knicks needed ‘lift’ in pulling rare NBA, G-League doubleheader|url=https://nypost.com/2025/01/02/sports/knicks-tyler-kolek-pulls-rare-g-league-nba-doubleheader/|website=nypost.com|date=January 2, 2025|access-date=January 2, 2025|last=Botte|first=Peter}} Teammates [[Jalen Brunson]] and [[Josh Hart]] have nicknamed him "The [[Michael Jordan]] of Rhode Island".{{cite web | last=McGowan | first=Dan | title=Time to accept it: Tyler Kolek is the Michael Jordan of Rhode Island | website=BostonGlobe.com | date=2025-01-31 | url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2025/01/31/metro/tyler-kolek-new-york-knicks-rhode-island-connections/ | access-date=2025-12-03}} In a December 23, 2025 game against the [[2025–26 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], Kolek recorded a career-high 20 points. Despite losing the contest, he played a significant role in the Knicks' performance, also posting 11 rebounds and eight assists.{{Cite web |date=2026-08-20 |title=Tyler Kolek Career High |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask/tyler-kolek-career-high |access-date=2026-08-20 |website=StatMuse |language=en}} On Christmas Day, Kolek scored 11 points in the fourth quarter to help fuel New York to a comeback victory over the [[2025–26 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cleveland Cavaliers]].{{Cite web|title=Knicks pull off monster comeback to steal Christmas game from Cavaliers at MSG|url=https://nypost.com/2025/12/25/sports/knicks-pull-off-comeback-to-steal-christmas-game-from-cavaliers/|access-date=February 21, 2026|website=nypost.com|language=en|date=December 12, 2025|last=Schwartz|first=Jared}} On June 13, 2026, Kolek and the Knicks won the [[2026 NBA Finals]], beating the [[San Antonio Spurs]] 4–1.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs. Spurs|website=[[ClutchPoints]]|last=Siegel|first=Brett|date=June 13, 2026|access-date=June 13, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/live-updates-2026-nba-finals-game-5-knicks-seek-first-title-since-1973|title=Recap: The Knicks win the 2026 NBA Marquette Golden Eagles guard, No. 22 Tyler Kolek|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/college/marquette/2022/03/09/get-know-marquette-golden-eagles-guard-no-22-tyler-kolek/6931701001/|work=[[Milwaukee Journal Sentinel]]|date=March 9, During the 2025–26 season, Kolek worked with a stylist to develop a reputation for his fashion sense.
